dialect.detail: JMA ORCA (Japan Medical Association standard receipt software) running on Linux, compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL. Program ORCS02 is a patient co-payment calculation subprogram for inpatient billing.
evidence: no EXEC CICS/SQL, no COMP-3, consistent with GnuCOBOL usage
34 COPY statements, 87 CALLs typical of ORCA modular architecture

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance billing system (ORCA) — inpatient co-payment (負担金) calculation subroutine for national health insurance, public assistance, and various prefectural subsidy schemes
purpose.summary: ORCS02 is a subprogram within the JMA ORCA medical receipt software that calculates patient co-payment amounts for inpatient claims. It handles multiple insurance combinations (national health insurance, disaster/self-pay, public subsidies), prefecture-specific rules, income-based limits, and consumption-tax rounding. It is called by higher-level billing programs and returns computed co-payment figures.

notable_features: 34 COPY statements for shared data structures
87 CALL statements to other ORCA modules
294 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
Japanese EUC/Latin-1 encoded comments (Kanji/Kana in comments)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — file-less, pure computation subprogram
No COMP-3 usage — all PIC 9 numeric fields
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments contain EUC-JP encoded Japanese text (rendered as mojibake in latin-1). This is standard for ORCA COBOL sources. The program is clearly production-grade JMA ORCA software with a detailed revision history spanning 2002-2005. Truncated at 16000 chars but structure and purpose are unambiguous.
